description.summary: warm the colours of a screen for the evening

protocol.description:
How trindle-nightlight tints the screens. A program says how much of its full brightness each of red, green and blue should keep, and the compositor sets the screen's colour tables to match, whatever size those tables are. Nothing here lets a program set any other kind of colour curve.
One program at a time holds a screen. When it lets go, or ends, the screen's own colours come back at once, so a tint never outlives the program that asked for it. Offered only to programs the compositor trusts with the screens.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: no more tints will be asked for

request.description: Tints already made are not affected.

request.name: tint
request.description: The tint is answered with "refused" if the screen cannot be tinted or another program holds it. Otherwise the screen is held until the tint is destroyed, and keeps its own colours until "warm".

entry.name: taken
entry.summary: another program holds this screen's colours

entry.name: unsupported
entry.summary: the screen's colours cannot be changed

request.name: destroy
request.description: The screen's own colours come back.

request.name: warm
request.description: Each share is how much of full brightness that colour keeps, from 0 to 65535. A share below a tenth of that is raised to a tenth, so a mistake can never turn a screen black. Does nothing if this tint was refused.

event.name: refused
event.description: The tint does nothing from now on. It should be destroyed.
